tab_venues.caption: \textbf{Journals and institutions.} Model-free difference-in-differences of scientist-year outcomes (treated country vs France + Germany, 2013--18 vs 2004--09; scientist and year fixed effects, standard errors clustered by scientist), stacked over the four fields and per field; plan written before the outcomes were computed. Journal quartiles and percentiles are article-weighted within each field: ``year of publication'' ranks journals by the normalized citations of that year's French and German articles (exploratory, not in the plan); ``current citedness'' uses OpenAlex two-year mean citedness as planned. Shares and percentiles in percentage points; institutions per article in institutions; treated pre-reform mean in parentheses. Lower panel (exploratory): scientists whose main affiliation in 2009--12 was covered by the policy or not.

tab_downloads.caption: \textbf{Pre-specified tests and headline estimates on both OpenAlex downloads.} The analysis plans were written against the download of 3--5 November 2026 (``original download''). The paper reports the latest download (``latest download''): the Italian, French and German works for physics, engineering and biochemistry were downloaded again on 8 November 2026, and all other data on 7--8 November 2026. Verdicts apply each plan's rule (negative with an interval below zero; placebo interval including zero; Russia's replication rule, in our reading: R1 and R2 met and no pre-trend in the fields with a significant model-free decline; for chemistry's mechanism tests C3--C5, ``consistent'' when negative with an interval including zero and ``not supported'' otherwise, and the plan's mechanism rule met if at least two of C3--C5 are supported or consistent and none is opposite). Rows marked $^\ast$ differ between downloads: chemistry's C3 (consistent only on the original download; on the latest $+0.001$, printed $+0.00$, not supported; a sign change of an estimate near zero) and hence the chemistry mechanism rule (met only on the original download), Russia's replication rule (met only on the latest download), engineering's all-returns estimate (significant only on the original one), biochemistry's model-free nearby-move estimate (significant only on the latest one) and the engineering and chemistry distant-jump weights (significant only on the latest one); all other verdicts in this table are identical. C3 and C4 use 100 scientist resamples and C5 300 on the latest download (100 on the original). Headline rows, not pre-specified for Italy, show whether the interval excludes zero (significant) or not (n.s.); the model-free nearby-move rows and the distant-jump weight rows were added after the main analysis. The original chemistry files were fetched on 5 November and the latest on 7 November; the raw files of both downloads are kept, with SHA-256 hashes (\texttt{data\_meta/raw\_manifest\_original\_download.csv} and \texttt{raw\_manifest.csv}). Co-authorship and journal outcomes are estimates without a single verdict because the plan's predictions differ by country.
